depth: The monocular depth visualization shows an indoor seating arrangement in several layers, progressing from a foreground wooden table (0.3–0.8 m away, bright grey), through a nearby round black table (1.0–1.8 m, mid-grey), to a third table in the background (2.0–3.5 m, dark grey to black). Within arm's reach in the foreground (~0.3–0.6 m), it distinctly separates the camera wearer's bottom-center smartphone, the handheld menu and cap at the lower right, the upright menu sign in the middle, and the grey-shirted person with a maroon bag seated immediately left (~0.4–0.8 m away, facing right toward the table rather than looking at the camera wearer) from the navy-jacketed person behind the left person (~1.2–1.6 m away, seated and facing right) and the black-shirted person to the right (~1.2–1.6 m, facing left). The grey-shirted person then leans forward into extreme close range in frame 5 (<0.3 m, bright white), appearing at the lower left as their head-mounted action camera projects directly before the lens and blocks the table's left side and the navy-jacketed person's torso. More clearly than RGB alone, the map conveys both the continuous 3D depth transition across the overlapping foreground and mid-ground tabletops and the abrupt close-range entry in frame 5. Nevertheless, it is unreliable for distant background patrons (>2.5 m), who blend into solid black, and for narrow boundaries such as the smartphone's top edge and the menu outlines, whose depths bleed slightly into the table surface's plane.
segmentation: The instance-segmentation view divides the scene into separate foreground and mid-ground people and tabletop items. It identifies the grey-shirted person at the lower left (~0.4–0.8 m away, within arm's reach) and the navy-jacketed person sitting about 0.6 m behind them (~1.2–1.6 m from the camera wearer), with both facing right, as well as people positioned across the right sides of the round tables (~1.2–3.0 m away) who face left or inward. The map separates the camera wearer's smartphone along the bottom border (~0.3 m away and within the wearer's reach) and follows both the upright menu sign on the center table (~0.7 m) and the handheld menu on the right (~0.5 m, reachable by both the camera wearer and the right-side person); these objects partly obstruct the black cap and tabletops behind them. Throughout the 5 frames, the mask for the left foreground person grows upward and rightward when their head and shoulders enter in frame 4 and then lean to within ~0.2–0.3 m in frame 5, progressively covering more of the navy-jacketed person and central table. Relative to RGB, segmentation more distinctly separates the overlapping patrons on the left and emphasizes the small, partly cropped background figures at the top boundary (~2.5–3.5 m away). Its class labels and frame-to-frame consistency are unreliable, however: the center standing menu sign and right handheld menu are variously mislabeled as a 'laptop', 'cell phone', or 'book' before their masks disappear entirely in frames 4–5; the foreground maroon bag and black cap are never detected; and the people on the right are split into inconsistent partial masks.
pose: Against a black background, the pose representation displays 2D skeletal keypoints, extracting hand locations and one mid-ground upper-body skeleton while leaving out every object and piece of furniture. Frame 1 contains only two magenta hand skeletons (~0.5–1.2 m away and about 0.5 m apart laterally): one corresponds to the grey-shirted person's gesturing left hand in the lower left, and the other to the navy-jacketed person's clasped hands above. Frames 2–5 also show a magenta hand skeleton at the lower right (~0.4–0.5 m, within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the right neighbor) grasping the handheld menu. Beginning in frame 2, a yellow upper-body skeleton is detected on the right (~1.2–1.6 m away) for the black-shirted person at the neighboring table. It depicts their torso turned left toward the room's center and their head facing left instead of toward the camera wearer, while their lower body remains hidden beneath the frame and behind the foreground table. From frames 2 through 5, changes in the camera view and the left foreground person's inward lean cause this yellow skeleton on the right to move upward and rightward toward the image border. In frame 4, the navy-jacketed person's torso and lifted arms (~1.2–1.5 m away, facing right) briefly register as another yellow skeleton. Although the pose view makes the detected subjects' finger articulation and torso direction easier to distinguish from clutter than in RGB, its overall reliability is poor: it entirely overlooks the nearest person on the left throughout frames 2–5, including when that person is <0.3 m away in frame 5; it does not detect the camera wearer's hands around the bottom-center phone; and in frames 2 and 3 it invents inverted torso links and incorrectly positioned facial keypoints near the lower-right hand.
